question.text:
Let $w, g$ and $n$ be propositions where $w$ is "I walk to work", $g$ is "I work in Gurugram", and $n$ is "I work at night". The sentence "When I work at night and I work in Gurugram, I don't walk to work" could be equivalently written using propositions and logical connectives as:

  1. $(n \wedge g) \Rightarrow  eg w$
  2. $(n \vee g) \Leftrightarrow n$
  3. $n \Rightarrow eg(w \wedge g)$
  4. $ eg(w \wedge g) \vee n$

• p = "All the world is apple pie"
  • q = "All the seas are ink"
  • r = "All the trees are bread and cheese"
  • s = "There is nothing to drink"
  • t = "Socrates was a man"
  • u = "All men are mortal"
  • v = "Socrates was mortal"

Consider the proposition: (( p ∨ t) ∧ (q ∨ u)) ↔ (s ∧ v)

Using the given truth values from the Socrates syllogism where:

  • t = T (Socrates was a man)
  • u = T (All men are mortal)
  • v = T (Socrates was mortal)
  • p = F, q = F, s = F

What is the truth value of the entire proposition? Enter 1 for TRUE, 0 for FALSE.
